additionalSurfaces.semantics: Accepted and ignored, including unknown fields; runtime logging belongs to the embedding API.
Only userLevel is consumed. Other input is ignored, not a supported interface/route configuration.
Validated by the dedicated REALITY parser when selected. Additional fields are currently ignored, not advertised as runtime features.
Dynamic domain-matcher keys map to an IP, domain alias or nonempty IP array; parser budgets and geodata expansion apply.
Dynamic u32 level keys map to POLICY_LEVEL.
Dynamic header names with string/null values and carrier-specific Host rules.
Dynamic header names with string/null Go template values; see HTTP_OUTBOUND.

Requires address, port 1..65535 and explicit XHTTP method/network. A separate bounded stream is parsed with paths remapped to downloadSettings; recursive downloads, stream-one and chaining are unsupported.

objects.notes: Value types, bounds and activation rules are enforced by the executable parser.
random, roundRobin, leastPing and leastLoad only; settings are interpreted according to the selected strategy.

Absent or null settings, or a null inboundTag, mean the empty tag. The handler never dials: it routes the connection again as if it came from an inbound with that tag, keeping its source, local address and user but no sniffed protocol or attrs, by the address the connection goes to and without routing's DNS lookups. Up to 8 loopbacks in a row; a longer chain fails the connection, where Xray-core recurses until it crashes. sniffing reads as an inbound's; enabling it is refused for now.
Absent or null settings and an absent response mean type none. The handler never dials: TCP receives the optional response and is closed; UDP datagrams are dropped.

type is required and case-insensitive: none, http (Xray's fixed HTTP 403 reply) or custom. custom sends customResponseData, standard padded base64 of at most 65,535 bytes; absent or null sends nothing. Other types ignore it. Null, empty and unknown responses fail closed, matching Xray.

At most eight servers. clientIp is an IP address every server without its own sends as the EDNS client subnet (/24 for IPv4, /96 for IPv6), as Xray-core sends it. enableParallelQuery asks every selected server at once; adjacent servers with the same policy race as a group, groups settling in order. Managed selection, cache/fallback policy and IPv4 fake IP only. hosts keys are domain rules as Xray-core reads them, plain text being the whole name; a "#N" value answers with DNS RCODE N from 0 to 15. Hosts and server URL semantics require the executable validator.
network/address/port aliases override rewrite* values. Deprecated nonIPQuery/blockTypes cannot be combined with rules.

Read as Xray-core v26.10.31 reads it. qType is a number or a comma-separated string of types and ranges; a reversed range adds no type, and a rule with no type answers every type. domain takes an array or a comma-separated string of domain rules, plain text being a substring; an empty list sets no condition. qtype and Reject are deprecated aliases with warnings; qType/qtype cannot both be non-null.

expectedIPs is an alias of expectIPs. clientIp replaces dns.clientIp for this server. domains takes an array or a comma-separated string of domain rules as Xray-core reads them, plain text being a substring. URL, address/port, query-family and domain/IP-filter combinations are checked by the parser.
IPv4 only. Positive poolSize must fit the usable pool after reserved addresses; ttl is positive.

TCP supports one fragment mask, one header-custom mask and one sudoku or xmc mask. Hysteria, mKCP, XHTTP H3, MASQUE over HTTP/3, XDRIVE over HTTP/3, freedom and WireGuard support one UDP noise, header-custom, Salamander and sudoku mask; mKCP also any number of mkcp-legacy masks, preserving array order. Any number of filter masks, in either list of any outbound, are validated and ignored, as Xray-core's client ignores them: their settings take blockedSourceIPs and allowedSourceIPs, IP rules as geodata.ParseIPRules reads them, whose geoip:, ext: and ext-ip: files and codes must exist, geoip:private included; field names match case-insensitively and unknown fields are ignored, as Go's JSON decoding does, so no grammar node fails closed there. After udphop or xicmp a filter is refused like any other mask: Xray-core accepts it there and fails every dial. On freedom every UDP flow's socket goes through the masks, which send only to the flow's destination and take replies only from it; on WireGuard the one socket to the one peer does, as Xray-core's FinalMask.DialUDP wraps both.
One noise, header-custom, salamander and sudoku mask on every UDP carrier, plus mkcp-legacy masks on mKCP and filter masks anywhere; type is case-insensitive.

mKCP only; absent or null settings mean both empty. No header: original obfuscation without a value, AES-128-GCM keyed by the value's SHA-256 with one. header is dns, dtls, srtp, utp, wechat or wireguard, case-insensitive; dns asks for the value as its domain, www.baidu.com without one, and the others ignore the value.
At most 16 packets, each up to 4096 bytes; reset is an idle interval in seconds, zero sends once per carrier peer. A nonempty script, which Xray-core runs in Lua, is refused until Lua is supported.

Xray array/str/hex/base64 packets or random length/randRange; delay follows each packet, at most 1000 ms per item and 10 seconds total. type exp (any case) reads packet as segments <b hex>, <r n>, <rc n>, <rd n> (random bytes, letters or digits, n a size or from-to range up to 65535), <t> (Unix seconds), <c> (the connection's counter) and <n> (8 random bytes), separated only by whitespace and built anew for each send; their largest packet must fit 4096 bytes here.

Hysteria, mKCP, XHTTP with exact h3 ALPN, MASQUE over HTTP/3, XDRIVE with exact h3 ALPN, freedom and WireGuard; on mKCP a header mask grouped with mkcp-legacy's, as in Xray-core. Password is 4..=4096 UTF-8 bytes. A packetSize range with a positive upper bound selects Gecko (1 <= from <= to <= 2048), which mKCP refuses for now; padding stops at 1452 bytes.

domainStrategy, or targetStrategy when nonempty, is deprecated and migrates to sockopt.domainStrategy, as in Xray-core. redirect is host:port as Go's SplitHostPort reads it; it replaces the destination address unless the host is empty, 0.0.0.0 or ::, and the port unless it is 0. userLevel selects the policy level of freedom's idle timer. proxyProtocol 1 or 2 writes that PROXY protocol header first; other values are ignored. finalRules are checked in order against each address freedom connects or sends to, and are ignored when freedom dials through dialerProxy. ipsBlocked is removed and ignored with a warning. noises, deprecated as in Xray-core, sends up to 16 datagrams before each UDP flow's first; the removed noise object is refused. Only the bounded tlshello fragment option is supported; other freedom settings fail closed.

type is rand, str, hex or base64, case-sensitively. packet is trimmed, and gives at most 4096 bytes: a length or range of random bytes for rand; the text itself for str; hex digits; or base64 in either alphabet, padding optional. delay is milliseconds, a number or range up to 1000. applyTo is ip (or all, or empty), ipv4 or ipv6, ignoring case.

action is allow or block, case-insensitive. network is a comma-separated string or array; names other than tcp and udp match nothing, and absent or empty matches every network. port and ip read as in routing rules, and ip may also be a comma-separated string. delay is seconds, an integer or min-max, defaulting to 30-90; blockDelay is its deprecated name, warned about, and wins over delay. logLevel is none, debug, info (the default), warning or error, case-insensitive, and is checked but writes no log here. delay, blockDelay and a nonempty logLevel belong to block rules only.

At most one fragment, one header-custom and one sudoku or xmc mask, plus filter masks anywhere: the fragment first when it and header-custom are both set, and sudoku or xmc last but for filters; type is case-insensitive.

Absent or null settings and sequences are empty. Before any other byte, the client writes clients[0], reads servers[0], writes clients[1], and so on, then reads the servers left; each server sequence must match. errors are read and never sent by a client.

At most one of packet (decoded by type: array, str, hex or base64), rand (random bytes in randRange, default 0-255, at most 65536 here), reuse (a captured variable) and transform; capture saves the item under a name of ASCII letters, digits and underscores. delay waits a random number of milliseconds before the item when its upper bound is positive.

TCP: the last mask, outermost on the wire; UDP: mKCP, Hysteria, XHTTP with exact h3 ALPN, MASQUE over HTTP/3, freedom and WireGuard, where the carrier lets the system fragment its datagrams. ascii is entropy (default) or ascii; customTable(s) are 8 characters of 2 x, 2 p and 4 v, ignored in ASCII mode; padding is a percentage range, each end at most 100. A snake_case name applies when its camelCase field is empty or zero. Unknown modes and malformed tables are refused here, where Xray-core fails every dial.

mKCP, Hysteria, XHTTP with exact h3 ALPN, MASQUE over HTTP/3, freedom and WireGuard; the last UDP mask, never with udphop, nor with sudoku on QUIC, freedom or WireGuard. Every datagram rides in the names of DNS queries to the resolvers, which reach the server's domain; polls keep queries waiting there for what it sends back. extraPoll is 0 to 3 polls after each packet and poll. At least one domain name and one resolver address are required.

names are the domains, each its own entry. lenLimit (0 reads 255) bounds a query's name and labelLimit (0 reads 63) its data labels; together they must leave 17 bytes per query. types are A (1), CNAME (5), TXT (16) or AAAA (28), one drawn per packet, TXT when empty; Xray-core refuses another only at dial, here it is refused. edns0 is 0 or 512 to 4096, the UDP size an OPT record advertises. A name with an empty label or one longer than 63 bytes is refused, where Xray-core's client panics at the first query.

addrs are udp:// (the default) or tcp:// with an IP address and an optional port, 53 by default. DNS over TCP sends each message after its two-byte length, which Xray-core's client fails to write. Names, https:// resolvers and their tlsConfig and quicConfig are not supported yet. worker is read and, as in Xray-core, only DNS over HTTPS would use it.

mKCP, Hysteria, XHTTP with exact h3 ALPN and MASQUE over HTTP/3; the last UDP mask, never with udphop, xdns or header-custom. The client finds its public addresses with STUN over the carrier's socket, asks the rendezvous at url to introduce it to the server registered under the realm name, punches a hole to the addresses the server reports and sends the carrier's datagrams to the one that answers. url is realm://token@host[:port]/name over HTTPS (port 443) or realm+http:// over HTTP (port 80), read with Go's url.Parse; its query and fragment are ignored. stunServers are one or more host:port entries, each port 1 to 65535. tlsConfig takes tlsSettings' fields for an HTTPS rendezvous; its fingerprint is checked and not used, as in Xray-core's HTTP client. ipMode is dual, v4 or v6, any other value reading as dual. Names are resolved like the outbound's server address.
Read as Xray-core reads it, enabled a boolean and timeout and lifetime 64-bit integers of seconds, but not acted on yet: no UPnP or NAT-PMP mapping is made, as when Xray-core finds no gateway.

mKCP, Hysteria, XHTTP with exact h3 ALPN, MASQUE over HTTP/3, freedom and WireGuard; the last UDP mask, never with udphop, xdns, realm or header-custom, nor with sudoku on QUIC, freedom or WireGuard. Every datagram rides in an ICMP echo request to the server, after an 8-byte client id, and comes back in its echo reply. dgram opens unprivileged datagram ICMP sockets; without it they are raw sockets, which need root or CAP_NET_RAW. ips are the server addresses, one drawn per packet; empty sends to the outbound's address, which must then be an IP address, else the core refuses to start: on freedom to each flow's destination, on WireGuard to its peer's endpoint. A zoned IPv6 address is refused, where Xray-core drops the zone and reaches nothing.

The last TCP mask, outermost on the wire. A Minecraft 26.1.2 login as one of the profiles, chosen per connection, then AES-128-CFB8 and the proxied bytes in custom payload packets. hostname is the handshake's server address, the server's IP address when empty. password derives the server's RSA key and is 1 to 113 bytes here, where Xray-core accepts a longer one and fails every login. profiles are required.
A signed profile the server holds too: username is 3 to 16 ASCII letters, digits or underscores; uuid is read as github.com/google/uuid reads it; texturesValue and texturesSignature are required.

mKCP, Hysteria, XHTTP with exact h3 ALPN, MASQUE over HTTP/3, freedom and WireGuard, never with udphop. mode is prefix (or empty), every datagram carrying the client's items in front and the server's checked and taken off, or standalone, the client's items sent alone and the server's answer awaited before the first datagram to a peer and five seconds after each answer; an unanswered request goes out again after a second on QUIC carriers, freedom and WireGuard, whose held send reads the answer in meanwhile. Case-sensitive, as in Xray-core.
As a TCP item, without delay.

op and at least one arg are required. Ops: concat, slice, xor16, xor32, be16, be32, le16, le32, le64, pad, truncate, add, sub, and, or, shl and shr; an unknown op fails when the connection evaluates it, as in Xray-core.
Exactly one of bytes (decoded by type), u64, reuse, metadata (local_port, remote_port, local_ip4_u32, remote_ip4_u32, src_port_u16, dst_port_u16, src_ip4_u32, dst_ip4_u32) and transform.

packets is tlshello in any case (the first write's TLS handshake record as smaller records, on a TLS/REALITY carrier or a raw freedom outbound), empty or absent (every write) or a write number or from-to range counting from 1 (those writes), whose writes go as raw pieces, each its own write, on any TCP carrier; a zero, negative or reversed range is refused. Positive lengths 1..16384, delays 0..1000 ms, up to 16 sequence entries, maxSplit 0..4096. A tlshello plan caps at 4096 records and 10 seconds; a cut write stages at most 64 KiB, 4096 pieces or 10 seconds of delays at once and continues in the next call.
Deprecated spelling; packets reads as FinalMask's. Same runtime bounds as FinalMask; interval is the delay range.
Timeout/window numbers are i32 clamped at zero. Header validity and Vision combinations also require core compilation.
Opt-in raw TCP race. tryDelayMs=0 disables it; bounds and transport combinations are validated.
acceptProxyProtocol is ignored on the client. headers must not contain Host. REALITY is unsupported.

Proxy-Authorization: Basic credentials, as Xray-core reads them: strings of any length, absent or null reading as empty; a later account replaces an earlier one with the same user. Credentials are redacted.

accounts (or users, read only when accounts is absent or null) lists at most 64 accounts, of which a request must name one; an empty list needs none. allowTransparent cannot be true. timeout is accepted for compatibility.

One flattened server or exactly one servers entry; mixing forms is rejected, while headers belongs to both. Credentials are absent (no authentication) or a user of 1..1024 bytes without `:` plus an optional pass of at most 1024 bytes, neither with control characters (RFC 7617 Basic); a lone pass is rejected and credentials are redacted. Level 0..255; email is type-checked and ignored. headers are set on each CONNECT after the credentials, so a Proxy-Authorization among them replaces theirs; a name is canonicalized, a null value is empty, and each value is a Go template that may name {{.Source}} and {{.Target}} and their .Address, .Port, .Network and .NetAddr. Other template actions, invalid names, control characters other than tabs and line breaks, more than 64 headers and values over 8 KiB are refused. CONNECT over raw/tcp with none or TLS, status 200 required: HTTP/2 when the proxy's TLS picks h2, HTTP/1.1 otherwise; TLS offers the ALPN Xray-core offers; no Mux or UDP. Without TLS the credentials travel in cleartext.
Nonempty address and nonzero port. users is absent, empty or exactly one entry.
user is required (1..1024 bytes, no `:`); pass is optional (at most 1024 bytes); neither may contain control characters; level 0..255. Email is type-checked and ignored. Credentials are redacted.
Linux transparent TCP/UDP interception only. Xray's protocol name tunnel is an alias. Firewall and policy routes remain operator-owned; no host network mutation.
followRedirect must be true; network tcp/udp/tcp,udp (default tcp). Destination rewriting and REDIRECT mode are unsupported.
Only raw/tcp with none security.
tproxy must be tproxy; optional nonnegative i32 mark also applies to source-preserving UDP replies. Requires Linux and socket privileges.

socks (alias mixed: SOCKS 5, SOCKS 4/4a CONNECT and HTTP CONNECT on one port), http and tun. Only loopback listeners unless allowUnauthenticatedLan is explicitly true. TUN settings have a separate compatibility surface.
Value types, bounds and activation rules are enforced by the executable parser.
Literal substring costs only; regexp=true is unsupported.

Enabled Mux supports VLESS, Trojan, Shadowsocks (2022 and AEAD) and VMess. Both concurrencies are int16. TCP concurrency 0 to 128 becomes 128, as in Xray-core v26.11.9, a larger one stays; negative disables TCP. XHTTP and VLESS Vision require negative TCP concurrency because the pinned server accepts only UDP children there. XUDP concurrency 0 shares TCP, negative uses native UDP, positive is taken as it is. UDP/443: reject (default), allow, skip. Each pool opens children on four parents with 1024 lifetime children each; exhausted parents finish their children, up to 16 parents in all.
Value types, bounds and activation rules are enforced by the executable parser.

freedom (alias direct), blackhole (alias block), dns, VLESS, Trojan, Shadowsocks 2022 and AEAD, VMess AEAD, SOCKS5 (CONNECT and UDP ASSOCIATE), HTTP/1.1 CONNECT, Hysteria 2 and a bounded WireGuard client subset. sendThrough is rejected whenever present, including null. targetStrategy migrates to sockopt.domainStrategy on freedom; other outbounds accept only AsIs. First outbound is the default. Tag graph validation is a later core compilation step.
Value types, bounds and activation rules are enforced by the executable parser.
Value types, bounds and activation rules are enforced by the executable parser.
Flags are modeled for compatibility; this is not the Xray statistics service.

Legacy form with migration warning; prefer sockopt.dialerProxy. Requires nonempty tag and transportLayer=true. REALITY chains fail parsing; cycles and additional carrier constraints are validated by core compilation.

Hysteria and XHTTP H3. congestion brutal (Hysteria only: Brutal at the lower of brutalUp and the server's announced rate, else BBR), force-brutal, bbr and reno; bbrProfile conservative and aggressive run a port of Xray's BBR sender, standard runs Quinn's BBR. Hysteria announces brutalDown as its receive rate. Hysteria and XHTTP H3 shape the handshake like Xray's ChromeParrot (quic-go's Chrome Initial packets, transport parameters and uTLS's Chrome QUIC ClientHello) unless disableChromeParrot is true; MASQUE never does. disableStatelessReset only affects Xray servers; maxIncomingStreams has no effect on Hysteria. Carrier compilation checks additional bounds.
acceptProxyProtocol is ignored on the client.
type may be absent, empty or none; request and response are ignored.

log is accepted and ignored. reverse, the legacy reverse proxy with bridges and portals, is refused unless null, with Xray-core v26.10.31's message: it removed the feature for the VLESS reverse proxy (an outbound's reverse). remarks (a string) and meta (an object) are subscription labels, such as Remnawave's, which Xray-core does not read; they are type-checked and ignored. Missing/non-array inbounds and outbounds currently normalize to empty lists. Non-object JSON roots also normalize to an empty model. Parse success alone does not establish runtime usability.
AsIs, IPIfNonMatch and IPOnDemand. Ordered field rules and bounded balancers only.

Read as Xray-core v26.10.31 reads it. type is not read. A nonempty outboundTag wins over balancerTag. inboundTag, domain, domains, ip and localOS take an array or a comma-separated string; domains replaces domain when both are given. network names other than tcp and udp match nothing, and any port given sets a condition, so 0, "" or a reversed range matches no port. A rule with no condition is refused. sourceIP (or source), sourcePort, localIP and localPort match the peer and the address the connection arrived on; user matches a SOCKS account by name or regexp:. protocol matches a prefix of the sniffed protocol: http1, tls, quic, bittorrent or fakedns. attrs maps lowercased attribute names, such as an HTTP request's :method, :path and headers, to regular expressions their values must match; a pattern that does not compile is refused. Domain/geodata, port selectors and aggregate budgets are validated. localOS matches the running platform as Go's runtime.GOOS names it: darwin on macOS, ios on Apple mobile platforms, android, linux, windows.

Read as Xray-core v26.10.31 reads it, every field checked even when sniffing is off. destOverride, domainsExcluded and ipsExcluded take an array or a comma-separated string. destOverride names http, tls (or https, ssl) and quic case-insensitively; fakedns and fakedns+others are accepted, as fake IPs are turned back into domains whenever dns.fakeIp is on. A sniffed domain in domainsExcluded, or a destination IP in ipsExcluded, keeps the original destination. excludedDomains is ignored after string-array validation.

Read and applied as Xray-core v26.10.31 does, to every socket the outbound opens, on Linux and Android or on Apple platforms. Every outbound TCP socket keeps alive after 45 seconds idle and every 45 seconds, unless tcpKeepAliveIdle or tcpKeepAliveInterval sets another number of seconds or a negative value turns keepalive off; a positive value with a negative one fails each TCP dial. On Linux and Android: mark, interface, tcpFastOpen, tcpCongestion, tcpWindowClamp, tcpUserTimeout, tcpMaxSeg, customSockopt and tproxy, in that order; tcpMptcp asks for Multipath TCP and falls back to TCP. On Apple platforms: tcpFastOpen, which their kernels refuse on a client socket, the keepalive settings, interface and customSockopt. The first option that fails stops the rest and is only logged, except interface, whose failure fails the dial. penetrate gives an XHTTP downloadSettings these options instead of its own. acceptProxyProtocol, v6only and trustedXForwardedFor are inbound options, type-checked and ignored. addressPortStrategy takes Xray-core's names, ignoring case: before a domain server is dialed, the first usable SRV or TXT record of its name, looked up as Go's resolver does from /etc/resolv.conf, replaces its address, its port or both; freedom and chained outbounds refuse it, and WireGuard's endpoint does not read it, as in Xray-core. dialerProxy selects transport-layer chaining; conflicts with proxySettings and missing/self/ambiguous targets are rejected. A dedicated freedom fragment handler is inlined before TLS/REALITY. happyEyeballs bounds and activation rules are enforced by the parser. domainStrategy takes Xray-core's eleven names, ignoring case; freedom, WireGuard and MASQUE read it, and other outbounds accept only AsIs.

Strings, read only when a socket is set up, as Xray-core reads them: an entry applies when system is empty or names the running platform as Go's runtime.GOOS does and network is a prefix of tcp4, tcp6, udp4 or udp6. level (default 6, TCP), opt and an int value are decimal integers, any text that is not one reading as 0; type int sets an integer, str sets value's bytes. An empty opt or another type fails, which stops the options after it.

RFC 1929 credentials; user and pass are strings of at most 255 UTF-8 bytes, absent or null reading as empty, as in Xray-core. A later account replaces an earlier one of the same user. Credentials are redacted.

auth is noauth (default) or password; other values are refused, where Xray-core reads them as noauth. users is Xray-core's other name for accounts, which replaces it unless null. password requires 1..64 accounts and makes the inbound offer only RFC 1929 username/password; accounts must be empty or absent with noauth. udp false refuses UDP ASSOCIATE with REP 0x07 as Xray-core does; an absent or null udp keeps it enabled, unlike Xray-core. ip is ignored; userLevel is parsed.

One flattened server or exactly one servers entry; mixing forms is rejected. user and pass are both absent (no authentication) or both strings of 1..255 UTF-8 bytes (RFC 1929); credentials are redacted. Level 0..255; email is type-checked and ignored. TCP CONNECT only over raw/tcp with none or TLS security; no Mux or UDP. Without TLS the credentials travel in cleartext.
Nonempty address and nonzero port. users is absent, empty or exactly one entry.
user and pass are required strings of 1..255 UTF-8 bytes; level 0..255. Email is type-checked and ignored. Credentials are redacted.

method takes priority over network. raw/tcp, ws/websocket, httpupgrade, grpc, xhttp/splithttp, kcp/mkcp, hysteria, masque, xdrive; security none/tls/reality. address and port are XDRIVE's: where its storage connections go instead of the URL's host, the port only when nonzero; other transports refuse them. Carrier/security combinations and inactive block handling require the validator.

allowInsecure=true is rejected. fromMitm is unsupported. Fingerprints, certificate pins and name constraints use parser validation. enableSessionResumption is a boolean with no effect on a uTLS-shaped handshake, which never resumes here or in Xray-core; with fingerprint unsafe, and on QUIC, rustls resumes sessions whatever its value.

1..8 distinct peers, at most 256 total allowed-IP prefixes, up to one local address per family, MTU 1280..1420; userspace TCP and MTU-sized UDP. Optional 32-byte PSK. remoteDNS accepts up to 8 IP literals, default Cloudflare IPv4/IPv6; destination DNS runs through the tunnel with bounded TTL caching, for the families of the local addresses, IPv6 first when there is an IPv6 one. domainStrategy is not read, of any value, as Xray-core v26.10.31 has none. streamSettings may hold sockopt and finalmask.udp: sockopt's options go on the UDP sockets, and its domainStrategy selects the address of a domain peer endpoint as Xray-core's does. UDP masks take one peer and go on its one socket, opened anew with their state at every rebind, as Xray-core dials it to the first peer's endpoint; udphop, realm and mkcp-legacy are refused. Nonzero reserved bytes and chaining are unsupported.

A nonzero IP/domain endpoint is required. Nonempty allowedIPs; at most 256 prefixes across all peers. Default allows both families. Longest prefix wins; identical normalized prefixes belong to the last configured peer. PSK accepts key encodings; absent, empty or all-zero means unset. Inbound user settings are unsupported.

A nonempty address and a nonzero port, as Xray-core requires. remoteDNS takes up to 8 IP addresses, scoped IPv6 ones refused; absent, null or empty means Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1, 1.0.0.1, 2606:4700:4700::1111 and 2606:4700:4700::1001. Destination domains resolve through the tunnel with the servers of the families the tunnel has an address of, IPv6 first when it has one. Requires network masque, security tls and no chaining or Mux; every TCP and UDP flow rides a CONNECT-IP tunnel through a userspace TCP/IP stack of MTU 1280, 16 TCP and 512 UDP flows a tunnel.

For the masque outbound only; Xray-core builds it under any network. host is the request authority, checked as Go's url.Parse reads it; empty takes the TLS server name with its port unless 443. path defaults to /.well-known/masque/ip/*/*/; {target} and {ipproto} and their query forms become *, and other braces fail. user and pass send Basic authorization; user takes no colon. headers are Go header fields, at most 64 values of at most 8 KiB, without Host or Capsule-Protocol, nor Authorization beside user or pass; User-Agent defaults to Chrome's, takes chrome, firefox, safari, edge, curl or golang as presets and empty to send none. HTTP/3 unless tlsSettings.alpn names h2 and not h3, then Xray-core's HTTP/2 client over TCP and TLS, which the uTLS fingerprint, sockopt and the TCP masks shape; over HTTP/2 the UDP masks and a TE header other than trailers fail. warp selects Cloudflare WARP (see its own entry). finalmask.quicParams and the UDP masks apply to HTTP/3: congestion brutal runs BBR, as in Xray-core; maxIdleTimeout defaults to 30 seconds and the keepalive to 10, or xmux.hKeepAlivePeriod when set, negative turning it off. The HTTP/2 keepalive is 45 seconds, or xmux.hKeepAlivePeriod when set, negative turning it off.

Cloudflare WARP, as Xray-core v26.10.31 reads it; no user or pass beside it. privateKey is the device's ECDSA P-256 key, PKCS #8 or SEC 1, in PEM or standard base64; publicKey is the endpoint's SubjectPublicKeyInfo in the same forms, any key Go's x509.ParsePKIXPublicKey takes; address takes prefixes or addresses, at most one per family, read and written as Go's netip does. host defaults to cloudflareaccess.com and path to /.
Version 2, one server, nonzero port; requires matching Hysteria transport and TLS. No chaining.

Absent or null keeps the defaults (mtu 1350, tti 50, uplinkCapacity 5, downlinkCapacity 20, cwndMultiplier 1, maxSendingWindow 2 MiB); null fields keep theirs. mtu 21..=8192, tti 10..=1000, cwndMultiplier at least 1, maxSendingWindow at least mtu. header and seed are ignored, as by Xray-core v26: mkcp-legacy masks replace them.

Version 2 and bounded authentication; stock QUIC TLS/h3, default bounded BBR configuration. FinalMask Salamander, UDP noise and udpHop are supported. Other QUIC/socket overrides, fingerprints and bandwidth overrides are rejected.
Hysteria2 only: numeric or comma/range ports with bounded hop intervals and protected socket replacement. Existing streams survive hops and host rebind. XHTTP H3 rejects nonempty hopping.

Hysteria or XHTTP with exact h3 ALPN, last UDP mask, which Xray-core dials outermost: mode is any comma-separated mix of intervalLocal, intervalRemote and perConnRemote; remotePorts and remoteIPs (IPs or prefixes, drawn only within the server's family). Default interval 30 seconds, minimum 5. A remote hop also takes a fresh local socket and always changes the port.

One flattened server or exactly one servers entry; mixing forms is rejected. uot and UoTVersion are sing-box UDP-over-TCP options that Xray-core does not read; they are type-checked and ignored, and uot true warns that UDP stays native. Methods are case-insensitive. SS2022: three blake3 methods; base64 PSKs, at most 8192 encoded bytes and 8 AES identity keys. ChaCha requires one key. Oversized keys retain legacy normalization; v26.10.21 requires exact-length keys, so portable profiles must use exact lengths. AEAD: aes-128-gcm, aes-256-gcm, chacha20-poly1305 and xchacha20-poly1305 with Xray aliases (aead_*, chacha20-ietf-poly1305, xchacha20-ietf-poly1305); nonempty password via EVP_BytesToKey. none/plain and stream ciphers are rejected, as in v26.10.21.

Nonempty address, nonzero port, level 0..255. Email, uot and UoTVersion are type-checked and ignored. TCP uses streamSettings; UDP is native encrypted datagrams of at most 8192 bytes, matching the pinned peer.

AEAD only. A non-null address is the simplified form, the server and its one user in these fields, and vnext is not read, as in Xray-core; otherwise exactly one vnext entry with one user. id is a UUID, or 1 to 30 bytes of text that name one as Xray-core's uuid.ParseString does. auto/aes-128-gcm/chacha20-poly1305; nonzero alterId rejected.
Nonempty address, nonzero port and exactly one user.
UUID, supported AEAD body cipher, zero/absent alterId; experiments accepts AuthenticatedLength and NoTerminationSignal, separated by |. Credentials are redacted.

One flattened server or exactly one servers entry; mixing forms is rejected. Password 1..4096 UTF-8 bytes. Empty/absent flow only. Verified TLS/REALITY required except private/test plaintext endpoints.
Nonempty address, nonzero port, level 0..255. Email is type-checked and ignored. Same security policy as flattened settings.

Read as Xray-core v26.10.31 reads it. A non-null address is the simplified form: the server and its one user are these fields, and vnext is not read; otherwise exactly one vnext server. Every field decodes in either form. seed is ignored. testseed sets the Vision padding parameters: the first four numbers when there are at least four. testpre keeps that many carrier connections opened ahead of the requests that take them, as Xray-core does, up to 64 here, and none with reverse. reverse makes the outbound the bridge of a VLESS reverse proxy (see its own entry); email is the user routing sees on the connections the server opens through it, and is otherwise ignored.

The bridge side of Xray-core v26.10.31's VLESS reverse proxy, in the simplified form only. tag must not be empty: the server opens TCP and UDP connections back through tunnels the outbound keeps open, and each is routed as if an inbound with that tag accepted it, with the address of the server-side client as its source and the outbound's email as its user. sniffing reads as an inbound's. A freedom outbound refuses these connections, holding them as a blocked final rule does, unless its finalRules allow them, and so does the freedom a dialerProxy chain ends on, for the hop before it and for the tunnel; a freedom dialing through dialerProxy applies no rule, and a chain under a shared Mux, testpre or gRPC connection is left as it is. Under an XHTTP link, and through a dedicated freedom fragment outbound a dialerProxy names, connections and the tunnel are refused before dialing unless that freedom's finalRules allow the server. The server's side, a VLESS inbound user with reverse, is not supported.
Nonempty address, port 1..65535 and at least one UUID user. Unencrypted public-address destinations are rejected.

Runtime selects the first user, where Xray-core wants exactly one. id is a UUID, or 1 to 30 bytes of text that name one as Xray-core's uuid.ParseString does. encryption defaults to none, where Xray-core requires it; non-none uses the bounded VLESS encryption parser. flow supports empty, xtls-rprx-vision and xtls-rprx-vision-udp443. testseed sets the Vision padding parameters, and testpre the connections opened ahead, up to 64. reverse is refused here, as Xray-core refuses it outside the simplified form. email is ignored; security is type-checked but ignored.
acceptProxyProtocol is ignored on the client. Host headers are normalized with a deprecation warning. REALITY is unsupported.

extra replaces rather than merges outer values except host/path/mode. Nested extra is inert. downloadSettings supports an independent XHTTP stack for packet-up/stream-up only; no recursive download. scMaxConcurrentPosts is ignored with a warning; h2Params (any JSON, Xray inbound only) is ignored. Rust-only h2StreamReceiveWindow: optional integer 65535..16777216 bytes, absent/null defaults to 4194304; H2 only, connection credit unchanged.

objects.context: xhttpSettings.xmux; splithttpSettings.xmux; effective extra.xmux; masqueSettings.xmux; xdriveSettings.xmux
objects.notes: Positive maxConnections and maxConcurrency are mutually exclusive. Ranges and default/zero semantics require parser validation. Under masqueSettings an all-zero xmux means one tunnel reused for 1800 to 3000 seconds, a tunnel takes maxConcurrency flows, cMaxReuseTimes counts flows and hMaxRequestTimes changes nothing, as in Xray-core. Under xdriveSettings an all-zero xmux means one connection reused for 1800 to 3000 seconds, four for google-drive unless tlsSettings.alpn is exactly h3, as in Xray-core.

Read as Xray-core v26.10.31 reads it; for VLESS with encryption only, without flow or testpre and with Mux on for every TCP and UDP connection (concurrency and xudpConcurrency not negative, xudpProxyUDP443 not skip). service is local, google-drive (Google Drive deprecated, with a warning), template or s3, case-sensitive. local carries each connection as files in remoteFolder, which both ends reach: an announcement in sessions/, then numbered segments of up to segmentBytes in streams/<session>/c2s and s2c, read back as Xray-core's server writes them. s3 keeps them in the bucket of its s3 object, template through the REST operations of its template value, and google-drive in the Drive folder remoteFolder names by id, with three secrets (client id, client secret, refresh token) and each session in rings of slots when it can make them; all over HTTP as Xray-core's Go client reaches them (the stream's TLS, xmux, address and port), over HTTP/3 when tlsSettings.alpn is exactly h3. The numbers are unsigned; zero takes Xray-core's defaults (512 KiB segments, 20 ms flush, 50 ms polls doubling to 500 ms after a 2 s eager window, 300 s session TTL, concurrency 8, 30 s hole timeout; for google-drive concurrency 64, a 10 ms flush and polls of at most 200 ms); segmentBytes is capped at 16 MiB and concurrency at 256. Over tlsSettings.alpn exactly h3, google-drive takes only the noise UDP mask and no service takes brutal congestion control.

Checked as Xray-core's ValidateS3Config checks it when service is s3: endpoint an http or https URL without user information, query or fragment; region a header value without '/', ',', space or tab, empty for us-east-1; a bucket without path separators; pathStyle true unless false, and virtual-hosted addressing needs a DNS endpoint and a DNS-compatible bucket. remoteFolder is then a nonempty relative key prefix, and secrets the AccessKeyID, SecretAccessKey and optional SessionToken.

validation.acceptance: Exactly the linked xray-config parser with the same geodata search paths. Warnings do not invalidate an input.
validation.fieldSemantics: Recognized keys include compatibility-only and restricted fields. Unknown keys fail when their grammar node is parsed. Activation, value types, aliases, cross-field constraints and budgets are enforced by the executable validator.
validation.geodata: Local files are read only when referenced; no downloads. CLI defaults match run (config directory, working directory, executable directory). --geodata-dir selects an exclusive ordered search list.
